why: ONE layout choice, three renderers. `scripts/render-social-cards.cjs` (Node, reads this file from dist/), `src/pages/admin/newsletter/socialCardCanvas.ts` (browser canvas -> JPEG, fetches the copy under public/ at /assets/img/shapes/card-variants.json) and the SVG export (a recording of that same canvas pass) all read this table, and all three pick a family through the SAME function: `familyFor()` in `src/pages/admin/newsletter/cardLayout.ts`. If they picked separately the admin would preview one composition and download another.
generated: GENERATED BY `node scripts/build-card-variants.cjs` — do not hand-edit either copy. The generator is what proves the geometry: it computes the ROTATED width of every box (rotate turns about the box centre, so a 560 px box at 14 degrees really eats 663 px) and refuses to write a table whose shapes fall off the ends of the strip or whose seam-crossing shapes do not actually reach across. Editing the JSON by hand skips all of that and nothing would complain.
shapes: Names refer to `shape-<name>.svg` in this folder. Real Glyiv geometry from the Figma frame SHAPE SAMPLE - see project-docs/BRAND-SHAPES.md. Never draw a replacement.
geometry: ⛔ `x` IS A POSITION ON THE FOUR-CARD STRIP, NOT ON A CARD. The four cards of one post are one 4320x1080 strip: x = 0 is the left edge of card 1, x = 1.0 is the seam between cards 1 and 2, x = 4.0 is the right edge of card 4. `w` is the box width in card pixels; the height follows from the file own viewBox, so nothing here can distort a shape. `y` is the box top as a fraction of 1080 and MAY be negative or exceed 1 - the top and bottom edges are not seams, so a shape is free to run off them. `rotate` is degrees about the box centre.
seams: ⛔ A SHAPE THAT TOUCHES A CARD EDGE IS CONTINUED ON THE NEXT CARD, AT THE SAME y, w, rotate AND alpha - BECAUSE IT IS THE SAME PLACEMENT. Owner, 20 August 2026: *"Card 1 ada shape sample semacam lingkaran, tapi saat saya swipe saya lihat itu tidak terhubung ke card 2 ... at least diberikan fullnya begitu jadi cardnya itu seperti berhubungan satu sama lain."* Before this table was rewritten only ONE shape spanned a seam (the bridge, hand-shifted by `x - 1`); every other shape was placed per card and free to run off the frame, which is what the owner saw. `cardLayout.shapesOnCard()` now slices the strip, so the discontinuity is not expressible. Three shapes per family cross one seam each - cover crosses 1|2, bridge crosses 2|3, closing crosses 3|4 - so all four cards are chained. `scripts/check-card-seams.cjs` proves it from pixels: it lays the four rendered cards side by side and compares them against the same strip drawn in one piece.
ends: ⛔ NOTHING MAY RUN OFF x = 0 OR x = 4. There is no card before the first or after the last, so a shape crossing an outer end is cut off with no possible continuation - the exact defect this rewrite removes, reintroduced at the two places nobody looks. `cardLayout.assertStripBounds()` throws on it and the generator refuses to write it.
familiesNote: ⛔ ONE FAMILY PER ARTICLE, CHOSEN BY HASHING THE SLUG - NOT ONE TEMPLATE WITH THE COLOUR SWAPPED. Owner, 20 August 2026: *"jangan hanya begini terus template kontennya, kreasikan agar semua artikel kita punya format card yang beda2 semua dan unique semua."* ⛔ THE PICK IS DETERMINISTIC (FNV-1a over the slug), NEVER `Math.random()` - a random pick would make the preview and the download two different pictures.
marks: The quieter second shape of each middle card - the per-card marker the owner asked for, at a LOWER alpha than the bridge so it reads as a mark rather than as a second bridge. Unlike the three seam shapes a mark is WHOLE INSIDE ITS OWN CARD, including its rotated bounding box: a mark that spilled onto the next card would be continued correctly and would stop being that card marker.
photo: Cards 1 and 4 carry the article own picture. Card 1 wears it as a low-opacity TEXTURE over the scheme ground; card 4 splits the frame with a divider and shows it at full strength in the panel. Which divider - slanted, straight, arched, notched, stepped, or a bottom band - is picked per article in `cardLayout.ts`, so the three renderers cannot draw six different dividers.
colourNote: ⛔ THE GROUND AND THE ACCENT ARE NOT IN THIS FILE, AND THEY USED TO BE PINE AND MINT FOR EVERY ARTICLE IN THE ARCHIVE. Owner, 20 August 2026: *"saya mau anda get kreatif, jadi postingannya tidak warna hijau melulu, kan di references/figma itu sudah ada color samplenya glyiv."* Colour is now picked per article by `src/pages/admin/newsletter/cardPalette.ts` from the ramps in `references/figma/COLOR.svg`, biased by the subject words in the slug. `paint` below stays a ROLE - `accent` or `quiet` - and the scheme decides what those two roles look like.
textSafeNote: ⛔ THE OLD "no shape may cross x=663" RULE IS GONE, AND ITS REPLACEMENT IS A MEASUREMENT. A shape that spans two cards MUST cross the text column - that is what spanning means. What replaced it: both renderers measure the worst-case background luminance under the actual text box and report the contrast ratio against the text colour, and the admin panel blocks download below 4.5:1. Text itself stays inside the 4:5 crop-safe band (x 108..972, `SAFE` in cardLayout.ts); shapes may cross it, words may not.
alphaNote: Alpha is per PATH, stated here rather than as a group opacity, because a canvas cannot do group opacity without an offscreen layer - so stating it per path is the only way the browser and Node renderers can agree exactly. It is deliberately NOT adaptive: the two renderers must produce identical motif pixels (scripts/check-social-card-shapes.cjs compares them). Photos adapt instead.
paintNote: `accent` and `quiet` are ROLES, not colours - see colourNote. In every scheme `accent` clears 4.5:1 against its ground and `quiet` is a tone of the ground itself.
compositionNote: ⛔ THE COMPOSITION IS NOT IN THIS FILE, AND THAT IS THE POINT. A family here carries SHAPES. WHICH cut the closing card takes, where the cover text sits, and whether it wears a keyline are picked per ARTICLE by `cardLayout.ts` from independently salted hashes of the slug, and the COLOUR by `cardPalette.ts` from a further independent hash. `scripts/check-card-count.cjs` counts how many different looks the real corpus actually produces rather than trusting the arithmetic.

families.name: arc-sweep
families.note: The open ring the reference feeds use as a single giant curve, run across the 2|3 seam; a square hatch bridges 1|2 and a second arc bridges 3|4.

families.name: ribbon-run
families.note: The three-knot ribbon of Feed - Day 2. Tall and narrow, so it crosses every seam as a vertical stroke rather than as a mass.

families.name: split-ring
families.note: The two-arc ring — 'two equal parts' — used at all three seams, so the split lands on a different card each time.

families.name: sprout-cross
families.note: The shape that crosses the seam in Feed - Day 1 and Day 3, used the same way — the widest set, so each seam carries a lot of the shape.

families.name: hatch-band
families.note: The bar diamond the owner used across the panel 3-4 seam of Feed - Day 1. The closing card puts the picture in a band under the words.

families.name: spool-turn
families.note: The stout waisted hourglass. The closing card mirrors: picture on the LEFT, words on the right.

families.name: chevron-flow
families.note: The double angle bracket — the quote mark of the frame. Widest closing shape of the eight, so the last card carries the most of it.

families.name: hourglass-seam
families.note: The two-storey hourglass, the one file with a see-through slit; the narrowest set, so the seams read as a thread rather than a wall.
